issue_context.title: Inconsistant naming of configuration options in modbus integration
issue_context.body:
### The problem

In the modbus integration, for *reading* values, the slave number is referred to as "slave: ..." in the configuration.yaml. For *writing* instead it is referred to as "unit: ..." in the modbus.write_* services. This is unnecessarily confusing. It should be either "slave" or "unit" in both places.

The underlying pymodbus uses "unit" as terminology.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.0b1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Modbus

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
modbus:
  - name: "pi_sauna"
    retries: 5
    timeout: 5
    type: tcp
    host: 192.168.123.123
    port: 502
    sensors:
      - name: "sauna_firmwareversion"
        slave: 247 <<<<<
        address: 1
        scan_interval: 120
        data_type: int16


light:
  - platform: template
    lights:
      sauna_leuchte_kabine:
        friendly_name: "Sauna Leuchte Kabine"
        turn_on:
          service: modbus.write_register
          data:
            hub: "pi_sauna"
            unit: 247 <<<<<
            address: 100
            value: 1
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

re-opened, the bot has failed here, we don't know why. It happens at times (unfortunately).

This is surely inconsistent, but changing it will break many configurations, so the preference is to keep it.

Remark the documentation states this as well.

It could be handled by adding the correct notation in one release together with a warning message for users that still use the old notation that it will be gone in say +3 releases (just like it was handled with the changes to defaults in templates).

review_comments:
We should avoid using this term, an use more neutral terms instead

<https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/a-z-word-list-term-collections/m/master-slave>
We use "slave" because the Modbus standard uses "slave", apart from that it has been used for a long time in the other parts of the configuration.
